Q: Excel vba insert new row(s) after a specific row based on another cell value A:

When inserting/deleting rows/columns on a sheet it is recommended to make the loop from the highest to the lowest value, because during execution the total number of rows/columns will continuously changes.

The below code will work based on this, assuming that the texts SalesX are in column A.

Sub InsertCellC4Rows()

For i = ActiveSheet.Range("A1").End(xlDown).Row To 1 Step -1
    If ActiveSheet.Cells(i, 1) = "Sales5" Then
        For j = 1 To ActiveSheet.Range("C4")
            ActiveSheet.Cells(i + 1, 1).EntireRow.Insert (xlShiftDown)
            'i+1 is because insertion is made before the actual row
        Next j
    End If
Next i


End Sub

Q: protoc3 grpc (go) code generation problem A:

The issue is in my view is straightforward:

Your protoc-gen-go-grpc is v1.6.1 generated code that references grpc.SupportPackageIsVersion9 and grpc.StaticMethod(), but your google.golang.org/grpc dependency in go.mod is an older version that doesn't have these symbols yet, so the incompatibility issue

The protoc compiler itself is indeed neutral here — the incompatibility is between the code generator plugin version and the grpc-go runtime library in your project.

The Fix

You need your google.golang.org/grpc module dependency to be v1.64.0 or later (that's when SupportPackageIsVersion9 and StaticMethod were introduced).

Run this from your project root:

go get google.golang.org/grpc@latest
go mod tidy

That should resolve both errors without touching the generated code.

Why This Happened

When you ran go install ...@latest, you got the newest generator plugins, which emit code targeting the newest grpc-go runtime. But your project's go.mod still pinned an older google.golang.org/grpc version. There's no single compatibility matrix published, but the general rule is: if you use @latest for the generators, also use @latest (or at least a recent version) for the runtime dependency.

Alternative Approach

If for some reason you need to stay on an older grpc-go runtime, you can install an older generator instead:

bash

go install google.golang.org/grpc/cmd/protoc-gen-go-grpc@v1.3.0

This would generate code compatible with older grpc-go versions (using SupportPackageIsVersion7). However upgrading the runtime is the cleaner path.

Q: Array methods simplification and best way of thorough understanding A:

There is the MDN documentation for JavaScript arrays:
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array

It has plenty of examples for everything, which could inspire you to come up with other use-cases. The easiest way you can understand is by writing code that uses arrays. Just write something. After you have written something you should ask yourself what could have been better about it.
If you really want to learn JavaScript, there is nothing you should skip.
Overthinking and not starting to code is a bigger problem than not understanding all techniques available. Just code something.

If there's a bug, we can help on https://stackoverflow.com/
If everything works but you still want a code review, try asking on https://codereview.stackexchange.com/
